text:
The conversation around Sidney Crosby has turned, and not toward his stat line. Sportskeeda carried a Penguins insider saying "The end might not be too far off," Montreal Hockey Fanatics wrote about a shift in his tone, and Markerzone reports the Penguins won't play hardball with him. It's all happening with Pittsburgh winless in four and Evgeni Malkin's name in trade headlines, which gives the week an end-of-an-era feel.

The numbers explain why people are asking. Crosby has 10 points in 16 games, and his scoring rate is 1.94 points per 60, down from 3.4 last season, when he put up 74 points in 68 games. At 5v5 the Penguins do about five points worse in expected-goal share (the quality of chances) with him on. But this isn't a collapse: four goals on 4.9 expected is about right, and his last ten games landed close to what we'd expect. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him 99th percentile in primary shot assists last season. Watch whether the puck starts finding his teammates' sticks again; that's where his points have always come from.
headline: Crosby's season, and the questions around it
